concepts.title: Meaning and Groups of Accounting Ratios
concepts.definition: A ratio sets one statement figure against another to expose their relationship; the family splits into liquidity ratios (short-term paying ability), solvency ratios (long-term debt cover), activity or turnover ratios (speed of using assets) and profitability ratios (earning capacity).
concepts.key_idea: Every ratio is just a division, but each division answers one specific question about the business.

solution_steps.explain: identify whether the question asks about paying ability, debt safety, asset speed or earning power
liquidity for current obligations, solvency for long-term debt, activity for turnover, profitability for returns
each ratio has one fixed numerator and denominator pair drawn from the balance sheet or profit statement

concepts.title: Advantages and Limitations of Ratio Analysis
concepts.definition: Ratio analysis simplifies statements, helps comparisons across firms and years, and spots weak spots quickly; yet it leans on historical, window-dressable figures, ignores price level shifts and qualitative facts, and means little without a standard or context to compare with.
concepts.key_idea: Ratios are as honest as the statements behind them and as meaningful as the benchmark beside them.
question_patterns: state the advantages of ratio analysis
what are the limitations of accounting ratios
how does ratio analysis help in comparing firms
why can window dressing distort ratio analysis
does a ratio mean anything without a standard to compare
how do price level changes affect ratio analysis

solution_steps.explain: simplifies figures, enables intra- and inter-firm comparison, helps forecasting and locating weakness
historical data, price level changes ignored, qualitative factors unseen, window dressing possible
a ratio needs a benchmark -- past figure, industry norm or rule of thumb -- before it can be judged

concepts.title: Current Ratio
concepts.definition: The current ratio divides all current assets by all current liabilities to show how many rupees of near-cash resources stand behind each rupee of near-term obligation, with two to one read as a comfortable norm.
concepts.key_idea: Inventories, receivables, cash, prepaid and advance items all count on top; payables, short-term borrowings and short-term provisions all count below.

current assets over current liabilities, expressed as so many times or as a ratio to one

concepts.title: Quick or Liquid Ratio
concepts.definition: The quick ratio strips the least liquid current assets -- inventories and prepayments such as prepaid expenses and advance tax -- out of current assets before dividing by current liabilities, giving a sterner acid-test of paying ability around the one-to-one norm.
concepts.key_idea: Only assets that convert to cash quickly may face the short-term bills; stock that must first be sold does not.

solution_steps.explain: deduct inventories and prepayments like prepaid expenses and advance tax from current assets
quick assets over current liabilities gives the acid test

concepts.title: Debt-Equity Ratio
concepts.definition: The debt-equity ratio divides long-term debts by shareholders' funds to show how much of the permanent financing came from outsiders; about two to one is the usual comfort line, and a smaller figure means more security for lenders.
concepts.key_idea: Borrowings plus long-term liabilities and provisions go on top; share capital, reserves, warrant money and pending application money go below.

find the proportion of long-term debt to shareholders funds

solution_steps.explain: long-term borrowings plus other long-term liabilities plus long-term provisions
share capital plus reserves and surplus plus money received against warrants (and pending application money)
the quotient shows the times-cover of owner money by borrowed long-term money

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Total Assets to Debt Ratio
concepts.definition: This solvency measure divides total assets by long-term debts to show how fully the asset base covers the long-term borrowing; a bigger figure means owners' money, not outside loans, financed the assets.
concepts.key_idea: A high cover tells the lender that even a shrinkage of assets would still protect the long-term loan.
question_patterns: calculate the total assets to debt ratio

find the ratio of total assets to long-term borrowings

solution_steps.explain: add non-current assets and current assets from the balance sheet
total assets over long-term debts gives the cover

concepts.title: Interest Coverage Ratio
concepts.definition: The interest coverage ratio divides profit before interest and tax by the interest payable on long-term debts, showing how many times over the earnings could pay the year's interest bill.
concepts.key_idea: Given profit after tax, climb back up: gross up for tax, add the interest back, then divide by interest.
question_patterns: calculate the interest coverage ratio from profit after tax
how many times does profit cover the interest on debentures
find the ratio of profit before interest and tax to interest

solution_steps.action: gross the profit back up for tax
solution_steps.explain: multiply profit after tax by one hundred and divide by the net-of-tax percentage
multiply the long-term debt by its interest rate
profit before tax plus interest gives profit before interest and tax
the quotient is the number of times interest is covered

concepts.title: Inventory Turnover Ratio
concepts.definition: The inventory turnover ratio divides the cost of revenue from operations by the average of opening and closing inventory to show how many times the stock was converted into sales during the year.
concepts.key_idea: Gross profit is removed first so the ratio compares cost with cost; a low figure warns of slow-moving or obsolete stock.
question_patterns: calculate the inventory turnover ratio from the given data
how many times did the stock turn over during the year
find the cost of revenue from operations and divide by average stock

build up the cost of revenue from purchases, wages and carriage

solution_steps.explain: opening inventory plus net purchases plus direct expenses such as wages and carriage inwards
opening plus closing inventory halved
the quotient is the number of stock turns in the period

concepts.title: Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio
concepts.definition: The trade receivables turnover ratio divides net credit revenue from operations by average trade receivables to show how quickly customers pay, and dividing the days in the period by it yields the average collection period.
concepts.key_idea: Debtors are taken before any provision for doubtful debts, and the collection period is just the period length split by the turnover.
question_patterns: calculate the trade receivables turnover ratio
find the average collection period from the turnover

how fast do customers settle their bills on average
should provision for doubtful debts reduce the debtors figure here

solution_steps.explain: total revenue from operations minus cash revenue from operations
opening debtors and bills receivable plus closing, halved, before provisions
credit revenue over average receivables gives the turns per period

concepts.title: Trade Payables Turnover Ratio
concepts.definition: The trade payables turnover ratio divides net credit purchases by average trade payables to show how fast the firm settles its suppliers, and the period length over the ratio gives the average payment period.
concepts.key_idea: A very low ratio can mean generous supplier credit -- or delayed payments that damage the firm's reputation.
question_patterns: calculate the trade payables turnover ratio

solution_steps.explain: opening creditors and bills payable plus closing, halved

solution_steps.explain: net credit purchases over average payables gives the turns

concepts.title: Capital Employed Turnover Ratio
concepts.definition: The capital employed turnover ratio divides revenue from operations by capital employed -- shareholders' funds plus long-term debts, or non-current assets plus working capital -- to show how much revenue each rupee of long-term funds generated.
concepts.key_idea: Higher turnover of the long-term fund base means the resources entrusted to the firm are being worked harder.
question_patterns: calculate the capital employed turnover ratio
find the net assets turnover of a company

solution_steps.explain: shareholders' funds plus long-term borrowings and debts

solution_steps.action: divide revenue by the fund base
solution_steps.explain: revenue from operations over capital employed gives the turnover

concepts.title: Gross Profit Ratio
concepts.definition: The gross profit ratio states gross profit -- revenue from operations minus cost of revenue from operations -- as a percentage of revenue, measuring the margin left to absorb all later expenses.
concepts.key_idea: A thicker gross margin means room for operating costs; a thin one exposes the firm to any cost rise.
question_patterns: calculate the gross profit ratio as a percentage
find the gross margin on revenue from operations

solution_steps.explain: revenue from operations less cost of revenue from operations
gross profit over revenue, times one hundred

concepts.title: Operating Ratio
concepts.definition: The operating ratio puts the cost of operations -- cost of revenue from operations plus operating expenses like selling, administration and depreciation -- as a percentage of revenue from operations, deliberately leaving out non-operating items and interest.
concepts.key_idea: The lower the operating ratio, the healthier the cost structure; it excludes financing charges by design.
question_patterns: calculate the operating ratio of a company
express cost of operations as a percentage of revenue

solution_steps.explain: cost of revenue from operations plus operating expenses

solution_steps.action: state it as a percentage of revenue
solution_steps.explain: operating cost over revenue from operations, times one hundred

concepts.title: Operating Profit Ratio
concepts.definition: The operating profit ratio is the mirror of the operating ratio: one hundred minus the operating ratio, or operating profit over revenue from operations as a percentage, showing the margin earned purely from operations.
concepts.key_idea: Operating profit is revenue less operating cost, so the two ratios must together exhaust the hundred percent.
question_patterns: calculate the operating profit ratio from the operating ratio

subtract the operating ratio from one hundred to get the profit ratio

do the operating and operating profit ratios always sum to one hundred
why is the operating profit ratio the residual of the operating ratio

solution_steps.action: take the residual of one hundred
solution_steps.explain: operating profit ratio equals one hundred minus the operating ratio

concepts.title: Net Profit Ratio
concepts.definition: The net profit ratio relates net profit -- usually after tax and including both operating and non-operating results -- to revenue from operations as a percentage, summarising the overall profitability of every rupee of sales.
concepts.key_idea: This all-inclusive margin is the base investors look at, and it feeds straight into return on investment sums.
question_patterns: calculate the net profit ratio of a company

solution_steps.explain: profit after all expenses and incomes, generally taken after tax

solution_steps.action: state it as a percentage of revenue
solution_steps.explain: net profit over revenue from operations, times one hundred

concepts.title: Return on Capital Employed
concepts.definition: Return on capital employed divides profit before interest and tax by capital employed -- the long-term funds of shareholders, debenture holders and long-term lenders -- as a percentage, testing how well the whole permanent fund base was used.
concepts.key_idea: Interest and tax are added back so the return can fairly be compared against the cost of borrowed funds.
question_patterns: calculate return on capital employed for the year
find the return on investment as a percentage
compute profit before interest and tax and divide by capital employed
what return did the long-term funds earn in the business
should interest and tax be added back before this return
compare the return on capital employed with the interest rate paid

solution_steps.explain: shareholders' funds plus long-term borrowings and debts
profit before interest and tax over capital employed, times one hundred

concepts.title: Return on Shareholders Funds
concepts.definition: Return on shareholders' funds (return on net worth) divides profit after tax by shareholders' funds as a percentage, answering the owners' own question of what their money earned inside the business.
concepts.key_idea: For leverage to help the owners, this return must beat the return earned on the whole capital employed.
question_patterns: calculate the return on shareholders funds
find the return on net worth of a company
divide profit after tax by shareholders funds and express as percent

solution_steps.explain: share capital plus reserves and surplus plus warrant money
profit after tax over shareholders' funds, times one hundred

concepts.title: Earnings per Share
concepts.definition: Earnings per share splits the profit left for equity shareholders -- profit after tax minus preference dividend -- equally across every equity share outstanding.
concepts.key_idea: Preference dividend must leave first; what remains belongs entirely to the ordinary shares.
question_patterns: calculate earnings per share of the company
find the profit available for each equity share
deduct preference dividend and divide by the number of equity shares
why is preference dividend removed before computing EPS
compute basic earnings per share from the profit statement
how does EPS guide the market price of a share

solution_steps.explain: profit after tax minus the preference dividend is what equity owns
divide by the number of equity shares outstanding

concepts.title: Dividend Payout Ratio
concepts.definition: The dividend payout ratio sets dividend per share against earnings per share to show what slice of the profit the company handed to shareholders and what slice stayed back for growth.
concepts.key_idea: A high payout favours income now; a low payout feeds future expansion through retained earnings.
question_patterns: calculate the dividend payout ratio
what portion of earnings was paid out as dividend
compare dividend per share with earnings per share
what does a low payout ratio say about growth plans
compute the retention implied by the payout ratio
state the ratio showing the share of profit distributed

solution_steps.explain: dividend per share divided by earnings per share, times one hundred
